charity = an organisation that helps people in need; giving help
volunteer = someone who works for no pay to help others
donate = to give money or things to help a person or charity
homeless = without a place to live
poverty = the state of being extremely poor
crime = an action that is against the law
steal = to take something that is not yours
burglar = a person who breaks into a building to steal
fine = money you must pay as a punishment
law = the system of rules in a country
obey = to do what a rule or person tells you
rights = things you are allowed to have or do by law
election = an event when people vote for a leader or party
vote = to choose in an election; one choice
government = the group of people who run a country
citizen = a person who belongs to a country and has rights there
community = the people who live in the same area
protest = a public event where people show they disagree
campaign = planned actions to change people's opinions or raise money
bullying = hurting someone again and again, with words or actions
cyberbullying = bullying that happens on the internet or by phone
equal = having the same rights and chances as others
unfair = not right or not treating people the same
help out = to give practical help
raise money = to collect money for a purpose
public transport = buses, trains and trams that anyone can use
traffic = cars and other vehicles on the road
pedestrian = a person walking in the street, not in a vehicle
rules = instructions that say what you may or may not do
polite = having good manners; not rude
rude = not polite; speaking or acting in an unkind way
respect = a feeling that someone is valuable; to treat them that way
generation = all the people of about the same age in society
responsibility = a duty to deal with something or take care of it
behave = to act in a particular way, especially well or badly
good manners = polite ways of speaking and acting
police station = the building where police officers work
arrest = when the police take someone away because of a crime
prison = a building where criminals are kept as punishment
thief = a person who steals
robbery = the crime of stealing from a person or place using force or threats
theft = the crime of stealing
vandalism = destroying property for no good reason
graffiti = words or pictures painted on walls in public
shoplifting = stealing goods from a shop
pickpocket = a thief who steals from bags and pockets in a crowd
witness = a person who saw a crime or accident
victim = a person who is hurt by a crime or accident
suspect = a person the police think may have committed a crime
law court = the place where a judge decides if someone broke the law
judge = the person who is in charge of a law court
guilty = having done something against the law
innocent = not having done the crime
illegal = against the law
legal = allowed by the law
identity card = an official card with your photo and personal details
nationality = the country you legally belong to
immigrant = a person who comes to live in another country
refugee = a person who leaves their country because of war or danger
asylum = protection given by a country to a person in danger at home
discrimination = treating people worse because of who they are
racism = the belief that some races are worse; unfair treatment based on race
prejudice = an unfair opinion formed without knowing the facts
stereotype = a too-simple idea about a group of people
tolerance = accepting people who are different from you
multicultural = including people from many cultures
human rights = basic rights that every person should have
freedom of speech = the right to say what you think, within the law
peace = a time without war
war = fighting between countries or groups with armies
army = the organisation of soldiers who fight on land
strike = when workers refuse to work to get better pay or conditions
demonstration = a public meeting or march to show you want change
petition = a document that many people sign to ask for change
slogan = a short phrase used to advertise an idea
banner = a long piece of cloth with a message on it
parliament = the group of people who make the laws of a country
prime minister = the head of government in some countries, including Poland and Britain
president = the head of state in some countries
member of parliament = a person elected to parliament
political party = a group of people with similar ideas who want to run the country
candidate = a person who wants to be elected
polling station = the place where you go to vote
ballot paper = the paper you mark when you vote
mayor = the person elected to lead a town or city
town hall = the building where local government works
local council = the group that runs local services such as bins and parks
tax = money you pay to the government for public services
news = information about recent events
newspaper = printed pages of news, sold daily or weekly
headline = the title of a news story, in large letters
broadcast = a programme sent out on TV or radio
advert = a picture or film that tries to make you buy something
poster = a large printed picture or notice on a wall
charity shop = a shop that sells used goods to raise money for a good cause
food bank = a place that gives food to people who cannot afford it
old people's home = a place where elderly people live and are looked after
orphan = a child whose parents have died
youth club = a place where teenagers can meet and do activities
scout = a member of a youth group that camps and learns outdoor skills
first aider = a person trained to give basic medical help
blood donor = a person who gives blood to help patients
neighbourhood watch = local people who watch for crime and help the police
queue up = to stand in a line and wait your turn
break the law = to do something illegal
keep the peace = to stop fighting and keep a place calm
tell the truth = to say what really happened
tell a lie = to say something that is not true
fair = treating people equally and in the right way
justice = fair treatment according to the law
duty = something you must do because it is right or the law
civic duty = something a citizen should do for society, such as voting
public place = a place that anyone can use, such as a park or station
private property = land or a building that belongs to a person or company
no parking = a sign that you must not leave a car there
speed camera = a camera that photographs cars going too fast
seat belt law = the rule that you must wear a seat belt in a car
age limit = the youngest or oldest age allowed for something
ID check = when someone asks to see proof of your age or identity
curfew = a time after which you must stay inside
noise complaint = when neighbours report that music or shouting is too loud
homeless shelter = a building that gives homeless people a bed and a meal
fundraiser = an event organised to collect money for a cause
sponsor = to give money to support a person or event
awareness = knowing that a problem exists and why it matters
global issue = a problem that affects the whole world
fair trade = buying goods so that farmers in poorer countries are paid fairly
